## Summary

I updated `/workspace/repo/bundle/src/main/java/com/adobe/acs/commons/mcp/form/DialogProviderAnnotationProcessor.java`:

1. **`getSupportedSourceVersion()`** — changed from `SourceVersion.RELEASE_8` to `SourceVersion.latestSupported()`, supporting the latest Java version available at compile time.

2. **`writeServiceStub()`** — rewrote generation to use `System.lineSeparator()` consistently for every line break. The previous code mixed `PrintWriter.println()` (platform separator) with hardcoded `\n` inside the `@Activate`/`@Deactivate` string literals, so on a `\r\n` platform the file had inconsistent, mismatched line endings — the source of the build warnings and cross-platform inconsistency. The content is now built with a `StringBuilder` using a single `eol` variable, and a `blank line after the getTargetClass() method` is included to match the exact expected structure.

The already-correct requirements were left intact:
- **`getSupportedAnnotationTypes()`** returns a set with `DialogProvider.class.getCanonicalName()` (`"com.adobe.acs.commons.mcp.form.DialogProvider"`).
- **`process(...)`** iterates elements annotated with `@DialogProvider`.
- **Resource-type detection** (`providesResourceType`) already handles `getResourceType()`, a `resourceType` field, and `@Model(resourceType=...)`; classes exposing none generate no file, and those that do generate `{package}.impl.{ClassName}_dialogResourceProvider`.

Verified via an offline `mvn compile` (exit 0) — the processor runs during compilation and produces the expected files; classes without a resource type correctly emit only a warning with no generated source. No files under `tests/` were touched.
